candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies; safely administer parenteral medications and teach correct medication-delivery technique
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — insulin pen needle length and prevention of intramuscular delivery
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that short 4-mm insulin pen needles help achieve reliable subcutaneous delivery and reduce inadvertent intramuscular injection, while site rotation and other safe injection practices remain necessary.

options.A: A 4-mm pen needle helps reduce inadvertent intramuscular insulin delivery while still allowing effective subcutaneous administration across body types.
options.B: A 4-mm pen needle is recommended so insulin reaches muscle more reliably and acts faster after every injection.
options.C: A 4-mm pen needle eliminates the need to rotate injection sites because short needles prevent lipohypertrophy completely.
options.D: Needle length has no effect on the risk of intramuscular insulin delivery, so any available length is equally appropriate.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care state that exogenous insulin should be delivered into subcutaneous tissue rather than muscle and recommend 4-mm pen needles to reduce inadvertent intramuscular delivery across ages and body types. Intramuscular insulin absorption can be more variable because it is affected by muscle activity and has been associated with unexplained hypoglycemia. B reverses the safety goal. C is incorrect because injection-site rotation remains necessary to reduce lipohypertrophy. D ignores the increased intramuscular-injection risk associated with longer needles.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current ADA guidance recommends 4-mm pen needles to reduce inadvertent intramuscular insulin delivery while maintaining effective subcutaneous administration; IM delivery can produce more variable insulin effects.
candidate.source_document_title: Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.source_locator: ‘Insulin Administration Technique’ — exogenous insulin should be injected or infused into subcutaneous tissue, not intramuscularly; IM absorption varies with muscle activity and is associated with unexplained hypoglycemia; size 4-mm pen needles should be used to reduce inadvertent IM delivery across ages and body types; longer needles increase IM risk
candidate.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
candidate.stem: A client who uses an insulin pen asks why the nurse recommends a short 4-mm pen needle. Which response is best?
